neurons in the medial temporal lobe respond selectively to images of people and objects.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of face recognition and object identification.
the study of visual object recognition in humans and nonhuman primates.

the MTL is the first area in the human brain where a representation of complex images can be recorded.
the human brain is able to represent invariant visual representations of complex objects and individuals.
the MTL neurons are able to recognize faces, objects and scenes in a way that is invariant to metric properties of the stimulus, such as size, position and viewpoint.

the MTL contains a sparse, invariant representation for visual stimuli.

neurons in the upper visual pathways of humans, as in monkeys, can respond to invariant visual representations of objects.
the human MTL contains a sparse, invariant and explicit representation of visual objects.
